seo.title: Oracle Database client for {devices}
seo.description: Connect to Oracle Database without Instant Client, run SQL and PL/SQL scripts, read DBMS_OUTPUT, and start Data Pump exports on the server.

header.title: Oracle Database client
header.lead: Run SQL and PL/SQL without Oracle Instant Client, and read DBMS_OUTPUT beside each result.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter a host, listener port and Service Name, or choose SID in <ui>Connection Type</ui>. Password sign-in supports the Normal, SYSDBA and SYSOPER roles, and a RAC SCAN listener, a shared server or a load balancer needs no configuration.

Native Network Encryption needs no setup: when the server asks for it, AES with a SHA-2 checksum is offered, and <ui>Network Encryption</ui> changes what TablePro offers. For TLS, choose Required for TCPS, or Verify CA or Verify Identity with a CA certificate; new connections start with SSL off.
On Oracle Autonomous Database, copy the host, port and service name from the TLS connection string, not the mTLS one, and set SSL to Required or Verify CA. Wallet files are never read.

bands.title: SQL, PL/SQL and transactions
text: PL/SQL blocks and stored units run as single statements, a / line ends a unit in a script, and compile errors carry Oracle’s messages and source positions. DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE lines show with the result of the statement that printed them, with no SET SERVEROUTPUT ON.

Each statement commits when it succeeds. Start with SET TRANSACTION, SAVEPOINT or LOCK TABLE to hold changes, grid saves included, until your COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Each user is a schema, and ⌘K switches the active one without reconnecting.

bands.title: Schema and Data Pump
text: Add, rename, modify and drop columns or create indexes in the Structure tab, with case-sensitive names quoted. Partitioned tables list their partitions, and subpartitions nest under them. Compare & Sync ({compareSyncTier}) compares Oracle schemas or data and writes / separators for SQL*Plus or SQLcl.
Server-Side Export starts a Data Pump job that writes a table to a DIRECTORY object on the server under your own privileges, so nothing lands on your Mac. Follow the job in DBA_DATAPUMP_JOBS.

moveData: Import {importFormats} files; a new table’s proposed name is upper case and fits Oracle’s length limit. Export tables or results as {exportFormats}, and a SQL export ends each routine and trigger with a / line, so SQL*Plus can restore it.
iphone: The Oracle driver is part of the app, and the form takes a Service Name or SID, the SYSDBA and SYSOPER roles and the Network Encryption setting. Browse tables as cards, edit rows that have a primary key and run SQL in the Query tab.

faq.question: Why do I see none of my application’s tables?
faq.answer: You probably connected to the container database. A pluggable database has its own service name, such as XEPDB1 inside XE; lsnrctl services on the server lists the names the listener answers for.

faq.question: Why does SET SERVEROUTPUT ON fail?
faq.answer: SQL*Plus commands such as SET SERVEROUTPUT ON, SHOW ERRORS and EXEC are not SQL, so the server refuses them. Delete them, since output is on from the moment you connect, and write EXEC p as BEGIN p; END;.

faq.question: Will an account with an old 10G password verifier connect?
faq.answer: Yes, though Oracle has deprecated the DES-based hashing it uses. Change the password with ALTER USER … IDENTIFIED BY and check that password_versions in dba_users then holds 11G or 12C.
